method: Complete current-snapshot static audit of all assigned 173 files. Every current file was reloaded and independently raw-byte SHA256/executable-bit checked against the audit9 manifest and audit8 report. All 171 TS/MJS files were freshly parsed with OXC; declarations, imports, guards, routes, schemas, test definitions and assertions were extracted. Literal schema/import existence, focused/todo markers and asynchronous assertion observation were checked across the complete assigned inventory. All 173 files are byte-identical to audit8, so prior same-checkout semantic review of their production/test/documentation content is explicitly retained, supplemented by the fresh manual reviews below. This is not a claim that all unchanged lines were manually reread. Fresh review covers provider/account/model selection, project creation, history/turn lifecycle, CLI exit and restart, terminal and connection ownership, receipts and authentication. It especially traces the newly changed web defaults retry through resource cancellation/generation, project routing, authenticated worker ownership, the single native defaults probe, cache key, timeout and confirmed cleanup. The new two-file web change also has a separate independent diff and regression-evidence review. No tests, source edits, network, browser, SSH, live requests or service actions were performed for this audit. Finally recomputed the full 1941-file snapshot and every frozen manifest hash/executable-bit entry; all still match audit9.
hashAlgorithm: SHA256 of raw file bytes; executable bits recorded separately

coverage.retainedPriorSemanticCoverage: All 173 unchanged files retain audit8 and earlier same-checkout production/test/documentation semantic analysis, including native fixture boundaries, platform ownership and recovery regression bodies. Current AST, route/schema/import/guard/assertion analysis and hashes cover every file again. This is substantive unchanged-analysis carryforward, not a claim of a new manual line-by-line read of every file or a new test execution.

freshManualFocusedReviews.focus: Defaults request validation and native-UID project resolution; canonical config/options/cwd cache identity, exactly one uncached probe, ephemeral thread/start without turn/inference, bounded timeout, owned process close before caching and finally cleanup; shutdown/read race and no reopening after close; cache-capacity/native process-exit assertions and documentation evidence limits. Cleanup failure keeps unknown/fatal. Re-reading defaults never clears unknown or starts a user turn.

Same-ID known-live status projection, legal terminal evidence priority, lifecycle fence across pagination, streaming revisions separated from turnRevision, cold interrupted retained, accepted-response revision guard and early completion before scheduler accept. Close/delete/revert invalidate terminal cache. Scheduler reads history and releases owned leases only after matching terminal evidence; no uncertain replay.

defaults/read remains a read without durable operation ID, projectId maps only to a registered cwd, worker requests bind authenticated live owner/channel and recheck before dispatch. Project creation positive acknowledgment persists registration even after disconnect; project/add read-only resolution requires the live owner before mutation. CLI exit drains definitive RPC replies before restart-ready exit75, and disconnected owners cannot submit late work.

Administrator login rechecks account version after password derivation; session/CSRF/client binding and logout revocation remain intact. Durable pending-to-dispatched-to-accepted/unknown transitions, positive acknowledgment handling, uncertain outcome preservation, bounded retained result capacity and exact original-operation recovery remain unchanged.

New error-local retry calls only defaults.refresh, keeps the button visible while pending, disables repeat clicks and uses the existing keyed/generation-fenced resource hook. Draft/provider/model/effort and permissions are unchanged. Separate independent review read the full new deterministic regression and author results, not rerun here. A defaults error alone is not asserted to universally block basic text; valid explicit choices can remain sendable, and unknown activity still blocks sends.

crossScopeReviews.resolution: A direct readonly defaults retry entry is now visible next to the defaults error for a new conversation. It does not refresh the provider model catalog, alter the shared hook/backend, clear draft or selected options, or bypass unknown/connection/activity admission. Author targeted 16-case evidence and typecheck are separately recorded; this reviewer did not rerun tests.
crossScopeReviews.observationBoundary: The prior live initial concurrent-probe error recovered after project navigation and explicit settings were sendable. The exact initial overlap was not reproduced; this repair improves discoverable recovery and does not claim a backend deadlock or universal inability to send text.

upgradeContract.failure: Stop at the first failed step and use its recorded recovery before proceeding.
upgradeContract.retainedCrossScopeEvidence: Deployment compatibility and management-lock independent reviews from audit7/audit8 are retained for unchanged deployment code. This web-only change does not alter strict final verify, retained legacy recovery context, initialization/management lock policies or provider migration order.
upgradeContract.finalAcceptance: The exact new candidate requires its separately authorized full CI and deployment/acceptance. Earlier CI8 and live observations refer to the previous 49f6 snapshot, not this e017 snapshot.

unexecutedIntegrations: No full or targeted test execution in audit9. CI8 passed the previous 49f6 source digest with 2388 distinct cases; these counts are not reused as validation of audit9.
No live administrator/provider login, browser, model inference, external MCP, SSH, deployment or main-service action in this audit.

Original hosted CI3 interruption cause was not reconstructed from its exact runner trace; the independently established history/live-state consistency defect and deterministic regression evidence remain separately documented.

The original live concurrent-defaults error was not deterministically reproduced from captured overlapping requests. Separate frontend regression controls capacity failures and recovery without asserting that original trigger.
